description: Canonical categories for reusable controls (Layer 5 of the Compliance-to-Architecture graph). A single control category can satisfy obligations from multiple authorities.

terms.definition: Authentication, authorisation, joiner/mover/leaver and privileged-access controls governing who can do what.
Controls protecting personal or sensitive data through classification, minimisation, masking, retention and lawful-basis enforcement.
Cryptographic controls protecting data at rest and in transit, including key generation, storage and rotation.
Collection, retention and analysis of telemetry and audit logs sufficient to detect, investigate and prove security or governance events.
Runbooks, on-call, severity classification, regulator/customer notification and post-incident review controls.
Controls governing how code, configuration and infrastructure changes are reviewed, approved, deployed and rolled back.
Identification, prioritisation, remediation and verification of vulnerabilities in code, dependencies and infrastructure.
Due diligence, contractual safeguards and ongoing monitoring of third parties touching in-scope data or services.
Site, facility and device controls protecting against unauthorised physical access, theft or environmental damage.
Lifecycle governance of AI systems: registry, risk classification, evaluation, post-market monitoring, human oversight, model cards.
Role-specific training, awareness and competence controls for personnel performing in-scope activities.
Continuity, disaster-recovery and operational-resilience controls covering RTO/RPO targets and tested failover.
